pEPR reports one Glass category while the recovery data splits re-melt from other. Any recycling rate per glass stream is therefore not computable from these sources, and a combined glass rate inherits the Paper / Card definitional caveat as well.

Table 2 splits each material's tonnage by agreed protocol, the agreement that fixes what share of a received load counts as packaging. Net received summed over protocols reconciles exactly to Table 1's UK reprocessing figure in all 84 year-quarter-material combinations, which is how the two tables were validated against each other.

The gross-to-net ratio varies enormously by protocol and is the single most consequential assumption in the dataset. In 2025 steel ran 1,198,621 tonnes gross through accredited reprocessors to yield 69,809 tonnes of packaging evidence, 5.8 per cent overall, and the '1+2 Mixed' protocol alone converts 241,047 tonnes gross into 1,326 tonnes net, 0.6 per cent. Steel packaging evidence is therefore largely a by-product of general scrap processing, and the tonnage credited rests on a protocol-assumed packaging fraction rather than on measured packaging. Glass, wood and the '100% Packaging' protocols sit at the opposite end at 100 per cent.

Table 3 names accredited operators that had not filed their quarterly return at the extraction date: 140 instances across the three years and 63 distinct companies. Non-filing concentrates in Q4 (17, 29 and 23 against 5 to 13 for other quarters) and exporters outnumber reprocessors roughly two to one. Published tonnage for a quarter is therefore incomplete to the extent of these operators' unreported volumes, which the table does not quantify.

The PRN revenue files state that glass other and wood are not split by operator type, because releasing it would breach EIR Regulation 12(5)(e) on commercially confidential information. The suppression is lawful and permanent, so revenue by accreditation type is unavailable for those two materials.
